equation_request.abstract: In this note we study the number of quantum queries required to identify an unknown multilinear polynomial of degree d in n variables over a finite field Fq. Any bounded-error classical algorithm for this task requires Ω(nd ) queries to the polynomial. We give an exact quantum algorithm that uses O(nd-1 ) queries for constant d, which is optimal. In the case q = 2, this gives a quantum algorithm that uses O(nd-1 ) queries to identify a codeword picked from the binary Reed-Muller code of order d.

specification.problem: Identify an unknown multilinear polynomial f of degree <=d in n variables over F_q exactly, using O(n^{d-1}) quantum queries for constant d. Scoped instance: q=2, n=3, d=2, with a phase oracle U_f|x>=(-1)^{f(x)}|x> and degree-1 Bernstein-Vazirani as the base subroutine.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful construction: q=2, n=3, d=2. Recursion on degree through discrete derivatives D_{e_i}f, with BV used on each derivative. Out of scope: general q (QFT over F_q), the paper's actual exact algorithm and optimality proof, the lower bound, and the Reed-Muller decoding details beyond the identification f <-> codeword. The recursion here is an assumed reconstruction, and the paper's algorithm may be more refined.

symbols.domain: positive integer, n=3 in the scoped instance
positive integer, d=2 in the scoped instance

symbols.meaning: primitive p-th root of unity, e^{2\pi i/p}, with p the characteristic of F_q; equals -1 for q=2

equations.label: Phase oracle
equations.description: Phase oracle form. For q=2 it is (-1)^{f(x)}. It is obtained from an XOR oracle by kickback with an ancilla in the Fourier state.
equations.justification: The sketch assumes the oracle model. The abstract only says 'queries to the polynomial'.
assumptions: Oracle convertible to a phase oracle by kickback

equations.label: BV base case
equations.description: For a degree-1 function over F_2, a single query returns a exactly. b is only a global phase, so it needs a separate evaluation, for example a query on |0> or a controlled version.
equations.justification: Standard Bernstein-Vazirani. The affine offset b is not recovered from this circuit alone.

equations.label: Derivative of a multilinear polynomial
equations.description: The derivative along e_i has degree <=d-1 and does not depend on x_i. It is implemented by U_f(shift by e_i)U_f^{-1}, which costs 2 queries. For q=2 the phase is (-1)^{f(x+e_i)+f(x)}.
equations.abstract_quote: identify an unknown multilinear polynomial of degree d in n variables over a finite field Fq
equations.justification: This is a derivative reduction, inferred from the family sketch. It is not stated in the abstract.
assumptions: Multilinear: each variable has degree at most 1
Phase oracle with its inverse available

equations.label: Query recursion
equations.description: Recursion giving the claimed query count for constant d. This is an assumed reconstruction that matches the abstract's O(n^{d-1}) claim.
equations.abstract_quote: uses O(nd-1 ) queries for constant d
equations.justification: The recursion is consistent with the claimed bound. The paper's actual recursion may differ.
assumptions: Each derivative query costs O(1) oracle calls

equations.label: Classical reassembly
equations.latex: c_S=\big[\partial_i f\big]_{S\setminus\{i\}}\ \text{for any } i\in S,\qquad c_\emptyset=f(0)
equations.description: The coefficient of S is read from the coefficient of S\{i} in the learned derivative. The constant term comes from a direct evaluation of f(0), via a query with a Fourier ancilla.
equations.justification: This follows from eq_3 and is a proposed combination step.

registers.name: x
registers.size: n*ceil(log2 q) = 3 qubits in the scoped instance
registers.role: input register, one qudit per variable; reused sequentially in the recursion

registers.name: anc
registers.role: phase-kickback ancilla in the Fourier state, only for the XOR oracle

specification.initial_state: |0>^{n} on x. For an XOR oracle, anc is in |-> (q=2).

steps.description: For d=2, n=3, and each i in {1,2,3}, build the derivative phase oracle on the other n-1 variables by fixing x_i=0: x -> shift e_i -> query U_f -> shift back -> query U_f^{-1}. Apply this to the remaining 2 qubits. The result is a phase oracle for the degree-1 function ∂_i f.

Run BV on each ∂_i f: Hadamards, derivative oracle, Hadamards, then measure the 2 qubits. This gives the linear coefficients c_{ij}. The offset of ∂_i f, which is c_{i}, needs one extra evaluation of ∂_i f(0)=f(e_i)-f(0), for example via a Fourier-ancilla query or a bit-test.
Evaluate f(0) by one query, to get c_empty. Reassemble all c_S classically.
Count total queries against the recursion bound.

specification.measurement: Measure the n-1 data qubits in the computational basis after the final Hadamards in each BV run. In Qiskit the counts string is little-endian, so qubit j is bits[::-1][j]. Do not measure in unitary tasks.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Map the measured bitstrings from each BV run to the coefficients c_{ij}. Reconcile the redundant estimates of c_{ij} obtained from i and from j, which should agree. Combine with c_i and c_empty into the full coefficient list, or the truth table for Reed-Muller decoding.
assumptions: Scoped to q=2, n=3, d=2 as one small choice, not given by the abstract
The recursion and the use of the e_i directions come from the sketch, not the abstract
Derivative oracles with fixed x_i=0 may need a query to f at shifted inputs, which a placeholder oracle gate acting on all n qubits permits
Constant terms are read by evaluations, not by BV phase
